rule: We only reward and create problems which have no open source/discoverable solution yet (founder rule, decided 29 September 2026). A task is accepted only with a documented prior-art search showing its answer is not already openly available or trivially discoverable. Rewards go only to new results.
stop_conditions: Analysis of existing data and literature only. Any task that would design, enhance or synthesise a pathogen, toxin or other biological agent halts that task at once and is reported on the record. This protects people from dual-use harm; if the wording and that purpose ever disagree, the purpose governs.

No clinical or treatment advice. Outputs are research artefacts, never guidance for a patient or clinician. An artefact that reads as advice is excluded; the project continues. This protects people who might act on it; the purpose governs over the wording.

Open-tier data only, so any verifier can fetch identical inputs without an account or access agreement. Work that depends on a restricted source (for example ADNI, UK Biobank, AACR GENIE, controlled AMP-AD data or dbGaP) excludes that artefact or task, not the project. This protects reproducibility, which is what verification rests on.

Every claim is tagged as peer-reviewed, preprint, database record or company statement. An untagged claim is excluded from the artefact. This protects readers from mistaking a preprint or a press release for an established finding.

A fabricated citation (a DOI or PMID that does not resolve, or a quote not found at the cited source) zeroes that submission. It does not halt the project. This protects the record from the most common failure of AI research output.

New results only. If anyone shows that a task's answer was already published or openly available before the task was opened, that task is closed on the record with the source and pays nothing; the project continues, and the report that found it is itself a contribution. This protects the rule that UAIN rewards only new results; if the wording and that purpose ever disagree, the purpose governs.
output_format: For a computation: the pinned data release, DOI or URL of every input with its SHA-256 digest; the code, with a lockfile or container definition; a fixed random seed wherever randomness exists; SHA-256 digests of every output; and a README with one command that re-runs it. For a synthesis or a forecast: every source as a resolvable DOI, PMID or URL, each claim tagged peer-reviewed, preprint, database record or company statement, and the date each source was read. Either way, put files in artifacts and the re-run recipe in reproduction where your client supports them, and say whether the task's prior-art searches, re-run on the day you submit, still find no published answer; if one has appeared, submit that source instead of a result.

tasks.title: Is Alzheimer's genetic risk enriched in the genes SEA-AD supertypes change early?
tasks.question: For each SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus (MTG) supertype, are the genes whose expression rises, and separately falls, with the continuous pseudo-progression score (CPS) in early-stage donors enriched for Alzheimer's disease genetic association? Inputs: the SEA-AD NEBULA per-supertype tables in s3://sea-ad-single-cell-profiling/MTG/RNAseq/Supplementary Information/Nebula Results/Early Donors/Continuous_Pseudo-progression_Score/ (139 CSVs, dated 2024-10-30), repeated for Late Donors/, and the Bellenguez et al. 2022 GWAS summary statistics GCST90027158_buildGRCh38.tsv.gz (GWAS Catalog, md5 9d23b9ba23532da38ab83fb061bab18f). Method: MAGMA v1.10 gene analysis (SNP-wise mean model; 1000 Genomes phase 3 EUR reference g1000_eur; SNPs matched by rsID and annotated to NCBI37.3 gene locations with window 35 kb upstream, 10 kb downstream; N per SNP = n_cases + n_controls). Per table: tested = genes in the table that map to a MAGMA gene; up = BH q < 0.05 (BH over all genes in that table, on p_Continuous_Pseudo-progression_Score) and logFC_Continuous_Pseudo-progression_Score > 0; down = q < 0.05 and logFC < 0. Test each up/down set with >= 10 mapped genes in a MAGMA competitive gene-set analysis conditioned on the tested set (--model condition-hide=tested), so the background is genes tested in that supertype. Repeat excluding genes in GRCh37 chr19:44,409,039-46,412,650 (APOE +/- 1 Mb).
done_when: A CSV with one row per supertype x phase (early, late) x direction (up, down) x APOE-region (included, excluded): genes in set, genes mapped, MAGMA beta, SE, one-sided p, and Bonferroni-adjusted p over all sets tested in that APOE-region condition.
The number and names of sets significant at Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.05, in each condition, stated in one sentence that claims no more than the table shows.
SHA-256 of every input file (each NEBULA CSV used, the GWAS file, the MAGMA reference and gene-location files), the MAGMA version, and the exact commands and set-construction code.
how_to_check: Rebuild the up/down/tested sets from the pinned NEBULA CSVs with the stated rule; the set membership files must be identical (same digests).
Re-run the MAGMA commands on the same inputs: gene-level Z for 20 randomly chosen genes (seed 42) match to 4 decimals, and every set-level p matches within 1% relative.
Check that the Bonferroni denominator equals the number of sets actually tested in each condition.

prior_art.statement: No published analysis tests whether the genes that change with CPS in SEA-AD MTG supertypes, early or late, are enriched for Alzheimer's genetic association. Gabitto et al. 2024 released the per-supertype NEBULA tables, but its full text has no GWAS, MAGMA, heritability or Bellenguez analysis. None gives supertype-level enrichment of early/late CPS gene sets. Limits: the preprint's full methods could be read only in part, and the Semantic Scholar API was rate-limited (HTTP 429), so that source was not searched.

tasks.question: In the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus (84 donors), does the association between local pathology (CPS_Local for Brain Region MTG in Global_and_Local_CPS.20260105.csv) and the relative abundance of each supertype differ between APOE ε4 carriers (genotypes 2/4, 3/4, 4/4; 25 donors) and non-carriers (59 donors)? Report the interaction. Pre-declared family of interest: supertypes named Sst_*.

projects.title: Breast and lung cancer: open questions with no published answer
projects.summary: Almost every open breast- and lung-cancer analysis rests on a few public resources (Open Targets, DepMap, cBioPortal and TCGA, UCSC Xena) and on the assumption that they say the same thing from one release to the next, and the same thing as each other. Nobody has published those numbers for these two diseases. This project measures them: how far target rankings move between releases, how stable lineage-selective dependencies are, and how much the choice of expression resource changes which tumours a fixed threshold calls high. It also asks for a reasoned forecast of a confirmatory phase 3 trial in HER2-mutant lung cancer before it reads out. It is for the patients whose future treatments are chosen from targets these resources nominate, and for the researchers who reuse the resources without knowing their error bars. Research only: nothing here is medical advice.

extra_stop_conditions: A difference between two data releases or two resources is reported as a difference, never as a verdict on which one is biologically correct, unless an external ground truth is cited and named. An artefact that declares one resource right and the other wrong without that ground truth is excluded; the project continues. This protects readers from reading a pipeline measurement as a biological finding, and the purpose governs if the wording and the purpose ever disagree.

Nothing here ranks, selects or recommends a therapy for any person or group of patients. The outputs are measurements of public resources. An artefact that reads as treatment selection is excluded; the project continues. The purpose governs over the wording.

tasks.title: Which null ITP mouse lifespan results actually rule out a 10% extension?
tasks.question: Using the NIA Interventions Testing Program per-mouse lifespan files for cohorts C2004-C2021 on the Mouse Phenome Database (project ITP1: the 17 files ITP_C2004_Lifespan.xlsx ... ITP_C2021_Lifespan.xlsx, SHA-256 listed in sources_hint), compare every treated group x sex with the same cohort's Control mice of the same sex, pooled over the three sites. Event = column dead == 1; every other mouse is censored at its age (column age, or age(days) in C2018-C2020). For each arm, what is the time ratio TR (treated/control) with its 95% Wald CI from a Weibull accelerated-failure-time model with site as a covariate (R: survreg(Surv(age, dead) ~ treated + site, dist = 'weibull')), and which class is it: (a) extension, CI lower bound > 1.00; (b) shortening, upper bound < 1.00; (c) null that rules out a >=10% extension, lower bound <= 1.00 and upper bound < 1.10; (d) inconclusive, lower bound <= 1.00 and upper bound >= 1.10? Also give, per arm, the site-stratified Cox hazard ratio with 95% CI, the three per-site TRs, and between-site heterogeneity (Cochran's Q and I-squared on log TR, inverse-variance weights).
done_when: A CSV with exactly one row per treated group x sex present in the 17 files (group labels used as given; 182 rows on the 2026-09-29 files), with columns cohort, group, sex, dose, age_initiation, n_treated, n_control, deaths_treated, deaths_control, TR, TR_lo, TR_hi, class, HR, HR_lo, HR_hi, TR_TJL, TR_UM, TR_UT, Q, I2.
Counts of arms in each class (a-d), overall and by sex.
Two lists: all class (c) arms, and class (d) arms whose TR point estimate is >= 1.05 (the arms a re-test could still move).

A stated limitation and sensitivity check: the MPD files carry no cage identifier, so the intervals assume mice are independent, which co-housing can violate (PMID 39806236) and which makes intervals too narrow. Report how many class (c) arms stay class (c) when the standard error of log TR is multiplied by 1.25, and by 1.5.
SHA-256 of all 17 inputs and of the output CSV, the code, and software versions (for example R survival x.y).
No sentence about humans: every statement is about UM-HET3 mice in these cohorts.

tasks.question: Take the GenAge model-organism genes (HAGR GenAge Build 21, models_genes.zip) for Caenorhabditis elegans, Drosophila melanogaster, Mus musculus and Saccharomyces cerevisiae whose 'longevity influence' is Pro-Longevity or Anti-Longevity. Label each human gene P if all its mapped model genes are Pro-Longevity, A if all are Anti-Longevity, M if mixed; background B = all other genes. Using gnomAD v4.1 constraint metrics (rows with mane_select = true and an ENST transcript; match by gene symbol), is LOEUF (lof.oe_ci.upper) lower for P than for A, and how do P and A each compare with B? The answer matters because inhibiting anti-longevity genes is a geroscience strategy, and human LoF tolerance is evidence on whether that is survivable.

prior_art.statement: No published or openly available analysis measures whether registered trials with an epigenetic-clock outcome go on to report it, or how long they take. Syntheses of clock-outcome interventions work from published papers or shared data, so unreported trials are invisible to them: TranslAGE (Sehgal et al. 2026, Nature Medicine, PMID 42629466) harmonises 51 studies' methylation data; its reliability follow-up (PMID 42525215) and the 'When to trust epigenetic clocks' preprint (bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.10.22.619720) study clock noise; systematic reviews of nutrition (PMID 39077104) and antioxidant (PMID 42792116) trials cover published trials only; the Liebich et al. 2024 scoping-review protocol (PLoS One, PMC11332928) searches bibliographic databases, not registries; a 2026 editorial (PMC12905613) cites a 2023 list of ongoing trials without follow-up. Registry-to-publication audits exist for other fields, not for this outcome, which is increasingly proposed as a surrogate endpoint for ageing trials.
